title: API incident protocols and synthesis v0
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working set of operational heuristics, quick protocols and synthesis notes for common API failure modes: client-visible request timeouts, 429s (rate limit/backpressure), degraded streaming responses (lossy or stalled streams), and elevated error rates (5xx spikes, model failures).

Audience:
Oncall SRE, first responders, tech leads doing evacs, and engineers doing postmortem synthesis. Not final policy — this doc gathers operator-proven shortcuts and open questions.

High-level decision tree (fast read):
1) Is traffic globally impacted or region-specific?
   - Check per-region request rate and 5xx counts in the last 5m. If only one region, suspect infra (AZ/IGW) or routing.
2) Is the failure primarily latency (timeouts) or errors (5xx/stream breaks) or throttling (429)?
   - Timeouts: look at p95/p99 tail latency and request queue depth.
   - 429s: look at quota, token bucket refill, and circuit-breakers.
   - Streaming degradation: inspect chunking, proxy timeouts, and connection resets.
3) Apply quick mitigations in parallel (below) while you investigate root cause.

Quick context checks (first 5 minutes):
- Dashboards: API surface p50/p95/p99 latency, success_rate, 5xx_count, 429_count, stream-abort-rate.
- Ingress: ELB/NGINX 5xx/timeout logs for connection resets or upstream timeouts.
- Serving runtime: average kv-cache hit rate, batch sizes, token throughput per GPU pool.
- Autoscale: check desired vs actual replicas for serving pools; look for queue/backpressure signals.
- Error breakdown: model error vs runtime OOM vs internal-service 5xx.
- Recent deploys: check deploy timeline (last 30m) for model binary, kernel, or infra changes.

Operator playbook (timeouts):
- Symptoms: client request times out (usually client 30s+), upstream latency high at p95/p99, KV caching cold, or GC/compaction spikes.
- Quick steps:
  1) Roll back any serving runtime or model deploys in the last 30m (if deploy coincident) OR route traffic to prior stable model variant.
  2) Lower sequence length and timeouts at proxy to reduce per-request work (temporary).
  3) Increase worker concurrency for streaming/generation pools if CPU/GPU utilization is low and queue is long.
  4) If heatmap shows high cold-KV misses, enable prefix cache warmup for the hot prompts (short-term cache pin).
  5) If OOMs are visible, temporarily reduce batch size or use quantized model variant.
- Commands and logs to inspect:
  - k8s: kubectl -n serving get pods -l pool=<pool> && kubectl logs -f <pod> -c runtime
  - runtime metrics: curl http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=rate(runtime_request_latency_bucket[1m]) (use dashboards)
  - infra: aws elb access logs / CLOUDWATCH for 502/504 spike buckets

Operator playbook (429s and backpressure):
- Symptoms: increasing 429_count with queues backing up, throttles emitted by gateway or runtime, client-side retries amplify load.
- Quick steps:
  1) Assess if 429s are originating at edge (API gateway) vs runtime. Look at x-edge-429 vs x-runtime-429 tags.
  2) If edge: temporarily raise per-customer rate limits only for premium tiers that need availability (use account list).
  3) If runtime: enable fallback routing to a lower-latency or lower-cost model variant (configured in routing policy).
  4) Apply short-circuit for non-critical endpoints (e.g., /metrics-exporter, /debug) to stop noisy clients.
  5) Throttle bursts: add a short global token-bucket penalty (few seconds) for heavy clients — coordinate with API gateway owners.
- Notes:
  - Avoid blanket global limit increases — those can degrade whole-cluster SLOs. Prefer targeted exceptions.
  - If clients are retrying with exponential backoff disabled, push back via stakeholder comms.

Operator playbook (degraded streaming):
- Symptoms: streams stall mid-response, partial payloads, chunk gaps, or repeated connection resets.
- Quick steps:
  1) Check proxy keepalive and streaming timeouts; increase to a safe short horizon if currently low.
  2) Inspect per-connection memory pressure on runtime; high per-conn memory indicates non-yielding generator loops.
  3) If pattern shows one model shard is failing, reroute streaming for that shard to alternate replica.
  4) If connection resets correspond to a network flapping event, engage infra (VPC or cloud provider).
  5) As fallback, convert streaming route to chunked non-streaming responses (trade latency for reliability).
- Quick commands:
  - tcpdump or connection logs at edge (ask infra)
  - streaming proxy metrics: stream_open_count, stream_reset_count per sec

Operator playbook (elevated error rates 5xx):
- Symptoms: steady increase in 5xx_rate, often model runtime exceptions, OOMs, or dependent service failures (e.g., vecstore, auth).
- Quick steps:
  1) Identify error signatures (stack traces or error codes). If model exceptions, mark model variant unhealthy and shift traffic.
  2) If dependent service failing, activate fallback (local cached embeddings, degraded features) and notify product.
  3) Scale up replicas if CPU/GPU saturation is the cause and autoscale is not catching up.
  4) If an infra or kernel regression suspected, rollback recent infra or runtime changes.

Escalation guidance:
- When to page: sustained customer-impacting SLO breach > 2m and no immediate remediation (traffic reroute) available.
- Who to page: primary on-call SRE -> runtime lead -> infra on-call -> product-ops if customer-facing changes required.
- Use bridge: create a temporary zoom/hangouts/bridge and put notes in the incident channel.

Communication templates (short):
- Initial slack post:
  "P0: API errors/timeouts observed across <region>. Investigating. ETA initial mitigation 15m. Paging SRE. (SRE-<jira>)"
- Customer-facing blurb (when internal mitigation applied):
  "We're currently experiencing elevated API latency affecting some requests. We've routed traffic to a stable variant and are continuing to monitor. We'll update in 30m or sooner."

Post-incident synthesis checklist (postmortem prompts):
- Timeline reconstruction: collect deploys, autoscale events, error spikes, and customer reports.
- Root-cause hypothesis and evidence: correlate logs to metric spikes.
- Action items: short-term (rollback, config flip), medium (autoscale tuning, circuit-breakers), long-term (routing resiliency, capacity testing).
- Owner + ETA for each action; verify in next SRE retro.

Operator heuristics and thresholds (suggested, tweak per-prod):
- Trigger paging if p99 latency > 10x baseline AND success_rate drops > 3% for 5m.
- Treat 429 rate > 1% of requests for a route sustained over 10m as service-impacting (investigate).
- If stream_reset_rate > 0.5% sustained, treat as degraded streaming; degrade to non-stream fallback if needed.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Should we expose per-customer backpressure metrics at the edge? (pros/cons: targeted mitigation vs privacy/scale)
- Add an automated runbook action to swap model variants in 2 clicks from Console. (UX request)
- Document concrete sample commands for Prometheus queries and a small CLI helper script to collect evidence (logs+metrics bundle).
- Add explicit regression tests for streaming under network jitter (lab work).

Appendix: helpful links and notes
- Common queries to copy into Prometheus/Grafana:
  - error_rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route)
  - latency_p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- Example incident keys to search in logs: model-exception, kv-miss, batch-timeout, oom-kernel
- Quick contact list: runtime-lead@redwood.com, infra-oncall@redwood.com, product-ops@redwood.com

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep this doc compact; move deep procedures into discrete scripts.
- Want to run a chaos test that simulates per-user burst retries and ensure our throttling protects core SLOs.

End of draft.

Revision log:
- v0 (2024-10-12): initial compilation of heuristics and oncall shortcuts.
- v0.1 (2025-03-02): added streaming fallback guidance and heuristics.
- v0.2 (2026-02-10): updated thresholds and added more comms templates.
